stories.title: 📜 Philemon
summaryBullets: This letter is from Paul, a prisoner for preaching the Good News about Christ Jesus, and from our brother Timothy. I am writing to Philemon, our beloved co-worker, (1:1).
and to our sister Apphia, and to our fellow soldier Archippus, and to the church that meets in your house. (1:2).
May God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ give you grace and peace. (1:3).
I always thank my God when I pray for you, Philemon, (1:4).
because I keep hearing about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all of God’s people. (1:5).
And I am praying that you will put into action the generosity that comes from your faith as you understand and experience all the good things we have in Christ. (1:6).
Your love has given me much joy and comfort, my brother, for your kindness has often refreshed the hearts of God’s people. (1:7).
That is why I am boldly asking a favor of you. I could demand it in the name of Christ because it is the right thing for you to do. (1:8).
But because of our love, I prefer simply to ask you. Consider this as a request from me—Paul, an old man and now also a prisoner for the sake of Christ Jesus. (1:9).
I appeal to you to show kindness to my child, Onesimus. I became his father in the faith while here in prison. (1:10).
Onesimus hasn’t been of much use to you in the past, but now he is very useful to both of us. (1:11).
I am sending him back to you, and with him comes my own heart. (1:12).
I wanted to keep him here with me while I am in these chains for preaching the Good News, and he would have helped me on your behalf. (1:13).
But I didn’t want to do anything without your consent. I wanted you to help because you were willing, not because you were forced. (1:14).
It seems you lost Onesimus for a little while so that you could have him back forever. (1:15).
He is no longer like a slave to you. He is more than a slave, for he is a beloved brother, especially to me. Now he will mean much more to you, both as a man and as a brother in the Lord. (1:16).
So if you consider me your partner, welcome him as you would welcome me. (1:17).
If he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to me. (1:18).
I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it. And I won’t mention that you owe me your very soul ! (1:19).
Yes, my brother, please do me this favor for the Lord’s sake. Give me this encouragement in Christ. (1:20).
I am confident as I write this letter that you will do what I ask and even more! (1:21).
One more thing—please prepare a guest room for me, for I am hoping that God will answer your prayers and let me return to you soon. (1:22).
Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you his greetings. (1:23).
So do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my co-workers. (1:24).
May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. (1:25).
crossRefs: Ephesians 1:15–16 — Thanksgiving for faith and love.
2 Corinthians 7:13 — Comfort and joy through others’ love.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אָסִיר לַמָּשִׁיחַ (ʾāsîr la-māšîaḥ, sense) — Greek: δέσμιος Χριστοῦ (désmios Christoû, NT) — Aramaic: אסירא דמשיחא (ʾasirā d-mešiḥā)
translationNotes.note: Paul describes himself as imprisoned on account of his service to Christ.

stories.keyTakeaway: Paul greets Philemon and gives thanks for his love, faith, and the refreshment he has brought to the saints.
